Liz — thanks for the questions and for the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front, then details below: 

- Marginal uptime cost: moving from 99.9% to 99.95% for the Priority Lane SKU is typically ~12–18% uplift on the support/retainer portion (not on token consumption). We can show exact numbers once we land on committed throughput. 
- Escalation routing: Priority Lane standard bundle includes 24/7 triage for Sev1 incidents with on-call handoff; 24/7 direct paging to a named engineer is part of the "Dedicated Oncall" add-on.
- SLA crediting: Credits are triggered by quantifiable SLO breaches (availability or latency windows) — not by support ticket creation alone. When a breach occurs we calculate credits per the SLA table in the draft PDF.

Details: 
1) Pricing mapping: attached draft (priority-lane-sla-draft.pdf) shows three packaging options: Pilot (99.9%, business-hours escalation, rolling credits), Standard Priority (99.9% + 24/7 Sev1 triage, retainer uplift), Enhanced Priority (99.95%, proactive runbook integration, faster MTTR targets).
2) Escalation coverage: our definitions: 
   - "Triage": 24/7 alert ingestion and acknowledgement within 15m, on-call triage engineer assigned within 30m.
   - "Direct Page": active paging to an on-call engineer (phone/SMS), included only in Dedicated Oncall add-on.
   - "Escalation": incident elevated to Sev1 with cross-team coordination and war-room; this is the event used for credit calculations when associated SLOs are missed.
3) Credits calculus: credits scale with outage duration and impacted tokens; examples are in the PDF. 

Next steps: Kimberly (pricing) and Jordan (enterprise SLAs) are looped to propose a tailored quote against your spreadsheet. If Arcadia wants overnight direct paging for certain integrations we can include a hybrid add-on with a reduced uplift for the pilot term.

Hi Liz — Rafael summarized things well. A couple of pragmatic notes from pricing to help you model costs for the pilot: 

- Uplift math: for a 12‑month pilot we can cap the Enhanced Priority uplift at 15% (rather than the 18% typical) if Arcadia commits to a minimum monthly token floor and a 3‑month calendar notice for early termination.
- Seat vs consumption: we recommend a hybrid: a small retainer to get predictable triage capacity + consumption-based token billing. That keeps unit economics fair while giving you the faster response windows.
- Trial credit concession: we can offer one-time goodwill credit equal to one week of retainer if an SLA breach > 4 hours occurs in the pilot (this is a special concession for pilot customers).

If that sounds reasonable I can prepare a line-item quote showing the hybrid model (retainer + per-token) with the 15% capped uplift for Enhanced Priority.

Kimberly Park
Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
